result.title: ARMED: Adaptive Retrieval-Augmented Medication Recommendation
result.summary: Medication recommendation requires jointly considering diagnoses, comorbidities, longitudinal patient history, and treatment interactions. Although recent retrieval-augmented generation approaches using language models have shown promise for clinical recommendation, most existing systems rely on fixed retrieval pipelines that cannot adapt to diverse clinical retrieval scenarios and may introduce noisy or irrelevant evidence. We propose ARMED, an adaptive clinical RAG framework that dynamically expands retrieval according to retrieval sufficiency and current-admission relevance. ARMED first observes the initial retrieval outcome and selectively performs supplementary or fallback multi-query retrieval when additional evidence is needed. The framework also incorporates a relevance gate that activates only clinically relevant same-patient history and organizes retrieved evidence into structured query-level clinical evidence. Experiments on MIMIC-IV demonstrate that ARMED consistently outperforms previous static retrieval baselines and improves overall medication recommendation quality. By combining locally runnable small language models with adaptive retrieval, ARMED supports medication recommendation without relying on external language model APIs or task-specific fine-tuning.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 ARMED 自适应临床检索增强框架：先观察首轮检索结果，按检索充分性与当前就诊相关性决定是否补充多查询检索，并用相关性门控只激活临床相关的同患者病史，将证据组织为结构化查询级证据，在 MIMIC-IV 上评估用药推荐质量。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「按检索充分性决定是否继续扩展检索」与「相关性门控筛选证据」可作为 LVR 中视觉证据筛选与 THINK/LOOK/STOP 停止决策的可核查方法线索，但属纯文本临床应用，迁移性需读者自行判断。
